summary: A GE Triton built-in dishwasher, made in February 2003. It is not part of the 2005 GE dishwasher recall. It has no pull-out filter: you keep it clean by clearing three spots in the tub floor, shown below.

label.location: inside the door frame, left side

fields.value: General Electric Company, Appliance Park, Louisville KY 40225
120 V, 60 Hz. Motor 1.8 A, other 6.4 A, total 8.2 A

age.summary: Built February 2003, so about 23 years old. GE serials start with a month letter (D = February) and a year letter (F = 2003 for a model of this era).

recall.summary: Not covered by CPSC recall 05-116 (2005, fire hazard). That recall covers GSD5560G units whose serial has G as its second letter, or starts with VF. Yours starts with DF.

care.title: Cleaning the filter
care.intro: There's no filter you pull out and rinse. A fine mesh screen covers the tub floor (part 502), a coarse dome sits under the lower spray arm (part 504), and a chopper blade in the pump grinds food small enough to drain.

steps.text: Wait 20 minutes after a cycle; the heating element can burn you. Pull the lower rack all the way out.
Pick out anything on the mesh screen or around the dome: glass, seeds, labels, bones.
Wipe the mesh screen with a damp sponge. A soft brush is fine. Never use scouring pads or harsh cleaners.
Spin the lower spray arm by hand; it should turn freely. Clear clogged holes with a toothpick.
steps.source: PartSelect parts diagram, part 501 (general care; this manual has no spray-arm section)

steps.text: For film or smell: run the longest cycle empty with no detergent. About 18 to 22 minutes in, open the door and pour 2 cups of white vinegar into the bottom.

care.when_to_call: it still won't drain after you've cleaned the air gap (the chrome cap by the faucet, manual p. 11) and run the garbage disposal.

facts.text: The dome and mesh screen are listed as no longer available, so don't force or crack them.
